extracted.intended_audience: immigration stakeholders (applicants, attorneys, advocates) and DHS/USCIS officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for DHS/USCIS officers and stakeholders on how to evaluate whether a noncitizen is likely at any time to become a public charge, explaining the statutory minimum factors (health, family status, assets/resources/financial status) and how evidence will be considered in the totality of the circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of medical examination reports
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering an applicant's health, DHS will consider any report of an immigration medical examination performed by a civil surgeon or panel physician where such examination is required, to which DHS will generally defer absent evidence that such report is incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will rely on findings made by civil surgeons or panel physicians as to whether any Class A or Class B conditions were identified, unless there is evidence the report is incomplete. DHS amended regulatory text consistent with this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the report of medical examination to be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The report will include, as required by HHS regulations and CDC Technical Instructions, any Class A or Class B medical conditions, 'the nature and extent of the abnormality; the degree to which the alien is incapable of normal physical activity; and the extent to which the condition is remediable . . . [and] the likelihood, that because of the condition, the applicant will require extensive medical care or institutionalization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil surgeons/panel physicians must note Class B conditions' potential to interfere with self-care, school, work, or possibly require extensive future treatment or institutionalization. DHS will weigh these specifics as part of the health factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class A/B conditions are not outcome-determinative alone
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere presence of any Class A or Class B condition diagnosed on a report of medical examination would not alone render a noncitizen inadmissible under this rule; DHS will take into account all factors identified in 8 CFR 212.22, including health, in the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No single condition (Class A/B) by itself determines inadmissibility; health evidence is weighed with other statutory minimum factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability cannot be sole basis for inadmissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant with a disability would not be found inadmissible on the public charge ground solely on account of that disability; a disability alone will never be sufficient basis to determine an applicant is likely at any time to become a public charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will not presume disability equates to likelihood of receiving public cash assistance or institutionalization; officers will be directed to assess whether a reported disability impacts the applicant's likelihood of becoming a public charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider disabilities only insofar as they impact health/public charge likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress did not direct DHS to consider disability as such; DHS will consider an applicant's disability only to the extent it impacts the applicant's health and thereby relates to the public charge analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS declines to exclude consideration of disabilities that are identified on a report of medical examination when those disabilities bear on health; but DHS will not consider disability in the abstract apart from health-related impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers must use totality of the circumstances framework
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will take into account all of the statutory minimum factors set forth in 8 CFR 212.22(a) (including health, family status, assets/resources/financial status) and make determinations based on the totality of a noncitizen's circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No factor (other than lack of a required Affidavit of Support under section 213A when applicable) is outcome determinative; DHS will not assign fixed weights to factors and will consider them together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants may submit other evidence relevant to health
rubrics_metrics.description: While DHS will not require applicants to submit initial evidence other than any required report of medical examination, an applicant is free to submit any other evidence relevant to the health factor for consideration in the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS added an express provision to consider any report of medical examination in the record but will accept supplemental evidence and may request additional information if needed prior to decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of family status via household size
rubrics_metrics.description: A noncitizen's family status will be determined using the noncitizen's household size, as defined in 8 CFR 212.21(f) (includes noncitizen, spouse residing with them, parents, children, unmarried siblings under 21 residing with them, other individuals listed as dependents on tax returns, and individuals who list the noncitizen as dependent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will determine a noncitizen's assets, resources, and financial status based on the household's income, assets, and liabilities to account for household contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family status not separately weighted; treated via household financials
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will not be assigning any weight within this rule regarding any of the statutory factors; a noncitizen's family status will be determined by household size and considered in the totality of circumstances rather than as a separately weighted positive/negative factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family ties that provide income/support are reflected through assets/resources; DHS declined expansive 'family unit' definitions beyond the household-size approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assets, resources, and financial status: household-based assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A noncitizen's assets, resources, and financial status are demonstrated by the income, assets, and liabilities of the noncitizen's household (excluding income from public benefits listed in 8 CFR 212.21(b) and income or assets from illegal activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Household includes defined members; sponsor income is included if sponsor is a household member, and portions of income provided by a non-household sponsor are included for the applicant's household income when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debts and financial obligations are considered
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider debts or other financial obligations when evaluating assets, resources, and financial status because obligations decrease accessible finances and affect likelihood of becoming a public charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS disagrees that debts should be ignored; officers will assess assets alongside liabilities in the totality of circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence flexibility and exclusion of illegal-source income
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will consider a variety of evidence to demonstrate income, assets, and liabilities and will not require specific evidence such as credit history or recent-asset-only documentation. DHS will not consider income or assets from illegal activities or sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS may request additional documentation if needed. Income derived from unauthorized employment may be considered (so long as it is not from illegal activities like drug sales), consistent with the 2019 Final Rule approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of unpaid/volunteer work
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS recognizes unpaid, volunteer, and other noncompensated activities but will not attempt to monetize them for assets/resources; instead, DHS may consider skills gained from such activities under the education and skills factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS cannot fairly establish a system to equate unpaid work to wages and fringe benefits; unpaid activities may support skills assessment rather than direct financial valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and special-status considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain populations are exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility (e.g., VAWA noncitizens, T nonimmigrants, and U nonimmigrants). H-2 nonimmigrants are generally not eligible for most public benefits and should report unlawful recruitment fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS notes statutory and programmatic exemptions and special considerations when applying the public charge analysis; officers should account for these exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of institutionalization vis-à-vis disability law
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will direct officers to take into account any evidence that the current or past institutionalization violates the Rehabilitation Act or any other Federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is intended to ensure fair and consistent treatment of individuals with disabilities and to avoid adverse decisions where institutionalization was unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: No minimum income threshold or prioritization of income
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS declined to establish a minimum income requirement or prioritize income over other factors; income is one element of assets/resources to be considered along with assets and liabilities in the totality of circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will not require demonstration of a wage level (e.g., three times federal poverty level) and will not give one factor primacy except the lack of a sufficient Affidavit of Support when required.
